fact: Cybernetica says that, to support its April 2024 to June 2025 pilot for Kenya's Ministry of ICT and ICT Authority, it put together an interoperability framework document built on the European Interoperability Framework, a high-level overview to help Kenyan organisations align; the document does not say the government adopted it (as_of is the pilot's end, June 2025; the document gives no other date).

The ICT Authority, under KDEAP, held a two-day workshop with ministries, departments and agencies on 6-7 November 2025 on Government Enterprise Architecture and the national e-Government Interoperability Framework, and says it will develop and finalize the national GEA standards and interoperability framework, so none is yet final.
system: National e-Government Interoperability Framework and Government Enterprise Architecture standards

fact: The report says Cabinet Secretary William Kabogo Gitau, speaking in New York around 21 September 2026 (the report says 'Monday' against its 24 September publication), drew on Kenya's Government Interoperability Framework as an existing basis for a cross-border service pilot; it gives no adoption date, instrument or content.

The ICT Authority's 2nd Edition Government Enterprise Architecture and Government Interoperability Framework sets out a framework for standardised data exchange between government agencies (interoperability charter, data, technical and metadata standards), but its approval date and document history are blank and its scope section says it is to be adopted by the entire government, ministries, counties and agencies; the document gives no date for the events and is dated by its 2023 publication year.
